pdf_row.text: Culp’s Hill, final charge Jul 3 | 10:00; noon | 10:00 | noon

basis.text: Geary, Kane, Rickards, Greene and Slocum (reports of July and August 1863) put the last Confederate charge and the enemy's retirement at 10.25 to about 10.30; the plan's 10:00 dates the Union counter-attack (Ruger, Hunt) and noon the end of all firing (Maulsby, Williams).

default.label: About 10:30: the last Confederate charge (begun 10:25 to 10:30) is beaten back and the enemy retires

animation.note: The last charge begins at 10:25 (Geary) and is over by about 10:30; the firing dies away to about noon (Maulsby, Williams). 10:00 and 12:00 stay selectable as the counter-attack and the end of all firing.

positions.label: 10:00: Ruger orders the counter-attack; Hunt and Meade round the recovery of the works

support.quote: This state of things continued until about 10 a. m., the enemy maintaining the attack with great constancy

witness.name: Thomas H. Ruger
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the First Division, Twelfth Corps (the right of the line); wrote on 5 Dec 1863

support.note: Ruger: until about 10 a.m. the enemy kept up the attack; in the next sentence 'at this time I received orders to try the enemy on the right of the line of breastworks' with two regiments. So his 10 a.m. dates the start of the Union counter-attack (Colgrove's charge), not the end of the Confederate charge.

support.quote: continued firing at intervals until 10 a. m.

witness.name: Henry J. Hunt
witness.role: Brigadier General, Chief of Artillery, Army of the Potomac (relays what the batteries and the Twelfth Corps reported)

support.note: Hunt, of the batteries on the hill behind the right: they continued firing at intervals until 10 a.m., 'when the infantry succeeded in driving out the enemy and reoccupied their positions' (the text layer misprints 'when' in the quoted tail, so the quote stops before it). The recovery of the works, not the last charge.

support.quote: at early daylight a spirited contest commenced, which continued until after 10 a. m.

witness.name: George G. Meade
witness.role: Major General commanding the Army of the Potomac (at his headquarters)

support.note: Meade: the contest on the right began at early daylight and continued until after 10 a.m. A lower bound only, which 10.30 satisfies; it says nothing of a counter-attack.

reason_not_chosen.text: Ruger's 10 a.m. is when he ordered the counter-attack; Hunt and Meade are relayed and round ('until 10', 'until after 10'; 10.30 satisfies Meade). The last charge came at 10.25 to 10.30.

inference.step: Ruger says about 10 a.m. for the point at which he ordered the Union counter-attack. Hunt, relaying twelve weeks later, gives 10 a.m. for the driving-out of the enemy, a round figure for the same recovery that Greene, Slocum and Geary place at 10.30; Meade's 'until after 10' is only a lower bound. None says the last charge ended at 10.

positions.label: Noon: the enemy's fire wholly ceased on the right (Maulsby, Williams)

support.quote: which it did until the enemy's fire wholly ceased, about 12 m.

witness.name: William P. Maulsby
witness.role: Colonel, 1st Potomac Home Brigade Maryland Infantry (Lockwood's brigade), in the rifle-pits on the right

support.note: Maulsby, the next day, from the rifle-pits on the right: his regiment held the front of the pits until the enemy's fire wholly ceased, about noon. This is the end of all firing on his front, after the last charge, not the charge.

support.quote: about 4 a. m. the 3d instant this regiment was ordered to attack a position of the enemy on the right

witness.name: William P. Maulsby
witness.role: Colonel, 1st Potomac Home Brigade Maryland Infantry

support.note: Names the day of the passage (the 3d instant) that leads to the noon of the next lines.

support.quote: at intervals until 12 m. , when the major-general commanding ordered the brigade to take

witness.name: J. M. Williams
witness.role: Colonel, commanding Nicholls' (Louisiana) brigade, Johnson's division, in the Confederate line before the hill

support.note: Williams (Confederate), from the line: his brigade engaged the enemy for four hours from early light 'almost without cessation, and at intervals until 12 m.', when the division commander ordered it back to the ravine. The end of his firing and his move, not a charge. His report is dated 28 August 1863.

reason_not_chosen.text: Maulsby and Williams (a Confederate) put the end of all firing, and the Confederate withdrawal, at about 12 m.; the last charge was over about an hour and a half before.

positions.label: About 10:30: the last Confederate charge (begun 10:25 to 10:30) is beaten back and the enemy retires

support.quote: was general on our line, and continued until 10.30 a. m., when the enemy retired

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps, in the works on the crest of Culp's Hill

support.note: Greene, nine days after, in the works: 'was general on our line, and continued until 10.30 a. m., when the enemy retired' (it began at 4 a.m.).

support.quote: At 10.25 o'clock two brigades of Johnson's division, having formed in column by regiments, charged upon our line on the right

witness.name: John W. Geary
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Second Division, Twelfth Corps (the division on the crest)

support.note: Geary: the last charge of Johnson's division began at 10.25; the next lines call it 'the last charge'.

support.quote: This final charge, made at 10.30 a. m., which was so eminently successful to us, resulted in the rout of the enemy

witness.name: John W. Geary
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Second Division, Twelfth Corps

support.note: Geary again, in his summary: the final charge, made at 10.30 a.m., ended in the rout of the enemy. Same writer: one line of knowledge.

support.quote: until about 10.30 o'clock, when the enemy made their last determined effort by charging in column of regi- ments. Their advance was Steuart's brigade, of Johnson's division

witness.name: Thomas L. Kane
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Second Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps (the right of the line, where the charge struck)

support.note: Kane, three days after, on the right of the line: after seven hours of fire, until about 10.30 the enemy made their last determined effort, led by Steuart's brigade. It dates the charge; his next lines say that after this repulse the battle was over, with a desultory fire for some time.

support.quote: About 10.30 a. m. the enemy advanced to charge us, Steuart's bri- gade leading

witness.name: William Rickards, jr.
witness.role: Colonel, 29th Pennsylvania Infantry (Kane's brigade), in the line

support.note: Rickards, the next day, from his regiment: about 10.30 the enemy advanced to charge, Steuart's brigade leading.

support.quote: The engagement continued until 10.30 a. m., and resulted in our regaining possession of our entire line of intrenchments

witness.name: Henry W. Slocum
witness.role: Major General commanding the Twelfth Corps (at the corps headquarters near Power's Hill)

support.note: Slocum's report (the day of the month of the dateline is unreadable in the text layer, 'August, 33, 1863'): the engagement continued until 10.30 and ended in our regaining the whole line. The corps commander's summary; it draws on his division and brigade reports, so it is a separate group but not an independent eyewitness.

support.quote: The First Brigade returned to our support at 1.30 a. m. on the 3d

witness.name: George S. Greene
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the Third Brigade, Second Division, Twelfth Corps

support.note: Same report: names the day (the 3d) of the passage that follows.

support.quote: from daylight until eleven o'clock, when his heroic troops are finally driven back completely repulsed

witness.name: Francis Marshal Pierce
witness.role: Author of a history of the battle, 1914 (not a participant)

support.note: Pierce in 1914: Johnson is left alone from daylight until eleven o'clock, when his troops are finally driven back. No source named; the reports of 1863 do not give eleven.
support.page_note: the text has no printed page marks in the layer; the passage is in the narrative of the third day, chapter on Culp's Hill

reason_not_chosen.text: A history of 1914 by a non-participant, no source named; the reports of 1863 give 10.30 for the last charge and the retreat.

inference.step: Pierce says Johnson held from daylight until eleven o'clock, when he was finally driven back; a later history documents only what its author wrote.

weighing.summary: The reports of 1863 agree on 10.25 to about 10.30 for the last Confederate charge and the retirement; 10:00 is Ruger's counter-attack order (with Hunt's and Meade's rounded, relayed figures) and 12 m. the end of all firing, so the three figures date three moments of one morning. Class settled.
weighing.who: Geary commanded the division on the crest and Kane the brigade the charge struck; Greene, Rickards and Ruger were in the works; Slocum and Hunt wrote from the rear and relay. Maulsby was in the rifle-pits; Williams, the only Confederate with an hour, was in the line before the hill. Johnson gives no hour.
weighing.when: All the main witnesses wrote within five months, and most within a month: Rickards 4 Jul, Maulsby 4 Jul, Kane 6 Jul, Greene 12 Jul, Geary 29 Jul, Williams 28 Aug, Slocum Aug, Hunt 27 Sep, Meade 1 Oct, Ruger 5 Dec 1863. Pierce (1914) is a later history. The written-down rank gives the best class to the 10.30 witnesses (reports within a month), and Ruger and Hunt, the 10:00 witnesses, wrote months later and relay.
weighing.where: Kane's brigade took the last charge on the right of the line; Geary commanded the division; Greene was beside them. Ruger's division was on the right and he gives the hour of his own order. Hunt and Slocum were behind the hill.
weighing.how_knew: Geary, Kane, Greene and Rickards saw the charge and give a clock reading; Slocum and Hunt report what their officers told them.
weighing.clock: All hours are Union clock except Williams, who is Confederate. The reported difference of about 20 minutes is not applied; it would not join 10:30 and noon.
weighing.independence: Three line witnesses carry 10.30: Greene, Kane with Rickards (his regiment is in Kane's brigade), and Geary as division commander on the spot. Geary's report of 29 July postdates the brigade reports and may draw on them, so Geary and Kane are not counted as independent of each other beyond their own observation. Slocum draws on his division reports; Hunt on his battery officers; Williams is the one Confederate and stands alone for noon on his side. Pierce is later and unsourced.

source_panel_text: About 10:30 on Jul 3: Geary and Kane, reports of July 1863, put the last Confederate charge beginning 10.25 to about 10.30, and Greene says the enemy then retired. The plan's 10:00 is Ruger's counter-attack order (Hunt and Meade round it); noon is when all firing stopped (Maulsby). Three other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 10:00 is when the Union counter-attack began and the works were retaken (Ruger, Hunt, Meade); the last Confederate charge came at 10.25 to about 10.30. It stays selectable as that event.

first_delegated.note: Its added 10:30 holds and becomes the default; its default 10:00 (Ruger, p. 781) dates the counter-attack, not the last charge. The tier documented holds for 10:30 (Greene, Geary, Kane).

failed_searches.where: OR27-2 R481 Johnson, R482 Steuart, R488 Walker, R495 Jones, R496 to R503 regimental reports of Johnson's division
failed_searches.query: a clock reading for the last Confederate charge or the retreat on the morning of Jul 3: Johnson says only that no further assault was made and that he held his position until 10 o'clock that night; the other reports were searched by clock words (a. m., o'clock, noon, 10 to 12) and not read to the end

failed_searches.where: OR27-2 reports of Daniel's, O'Neal's (Rodes's division) and Smith's brigades (R-numbers of the index)
failed_searches.query: any hour for the charge: no report of these brigades was read

failed_searches.where: all local books and papers (find_passage --all, class primary, book, official)
failed_searches.query: Culp, Johnson, Steuart, Stonewall Brigade, Greene, Geary, Kane within 250 characters of 10 or 11 o'clock or a. m. and retired, repulsed, charge, ceased: only Pierce 1914 (eleven o'clock) was new

what_would_change_it: A report of Johnson's, Steuart's, Walker's or Rodes's division that gives an hour with its clock for the last charge, or a signal or telegraph message timed on the morning of Jul 3, would test the Union hours; a contradiction among Union reports on 10.30 would reopen the class.
